headline: OPTICAL LENSES REBOUND

move_context.summary: A fictional lens basket is up 3.4% after a 12% pullback. A local report attributes the rebound to a possible handset upgrade cycle; positioning after the de-rating is an alternative explanation, not an independently established catalyst.

fundamental_hook: An illustrative broker thesis links more complex optics to higher lens ASP. That is distinct from a unit-volume recovery; a proposed adjacent product contributes no revenue until the stated future production date.
mixed_evidence: Some channel lead times are shorter than the comparable launch, a possible demand warning.
A different model mix and launch calendar may distort the year-on-year comparison.
A separate carrier check shows later delivery dates for selected models, providing a counterpoint rather than resolving the demand question.
implications: EXAMPLE-MODULE KS Equity: content per device may rise if the higher-spec camera mix persists.
EXAMPLE-SENSOR JP Equity: exposure is mainly to unit volumes, so higher lens ASP alone does not establish upside.
watch: 21 Sep: first deliveries in this synthetic scenario; resale pricing is a suggested demand proxy, not conclusive evidence.
Next monthly sales release: compare supplier revenue with the broker's volume and ASP assumptions.
